digest.component_or_area: review-bot container IAM and Bedrock integration
propositions: The review-bot container must obtain short-lived credentials authorized for Bedrock from the existing rebar-gerrit-instance-role via IMDSv2, not via long-term API keys in SSM or a separate credential broker.

The Converse API authorizes against bedrock:InvokeModel (not bedrock:Converse), which is proven only by a real call from the scoped role; policy simulation alone cannot distinguish the action the service checks from the action the policy language permits.
Scoped inline policies for Bedrock must live in a separate iam_s7.tf file to honor the single-owner contract stated in iam.tf:4-9; iam.tf itself must not be modified by this story.

Cross-region inference profiles require wildcard region in both the foundation-model ARN and the inference-profile ARN; pinning the region or profile prefix would silently deny valid model IDs at runtime.
If IMDSv2 token requests fail from the review-bot container, http_put_response_hop_limit must be raised to 2 with http_tokens still required, and the bounded exposure must be documented in ADR 0046.

The least-privilege grant (bedrock:InvokeModel and bedrock:InvokeModelWithResponseStream scoped to Claude models only) must be verified by simulate-principal-policy plus a real from-instance Converse call plus a negative control denying non-Claude models, never from an identity holding bedrock:*.
